tools.name: stream_list
tools.description: List streams filtered by status, id, name and return their quick overview.

tools.name: stream_get
tools.description: Get stream (loop) information, use it to get its current state, enabled destinations and configuration.

tools.name: stream_create
tools.description: Create a new stream. You can create stream for pre-recorded videos or live scene stream (supports pre-recorded videos too). Live scene is used for more complex setups to include features like overlays, layouts, multiple inputs, and so on. Afterwards, use stream_update to set its quality and framerat

tools.name: stream_create_copy
tools.description: Copies a stream into a new draft: its settings, playlists (items and playing order), linked destinations and YouTube settings; never its schedule. A scene stream's copy plays the same scene as the original, not a copy of it: editing the scene changes both. `copied` lists what was carried over.

tools.name: stream_update
tools.description: Updates stream configuration. Quality and framerate: not while live.

tools.name: stream_update_youtube_broadcast_settings
tools.description: Updates YouTube broadcast settings (only when has linked YouTube channel using Oauth).

tools.name: stream_remove
tools.description: Deletes a stream with its playlists and schedule. Uploaded media and destinations are kept. A scene stream's scene is deleted with it unless another stream plays that scene. Refused with STREAM_LIVE while it is on air: stop it first. A stream already deleted is NOT_FOUND.

tools.name: stream_add_output
tools.description: Links a destination to the stream. Up to 5 per stream, disabled ones included, and one YouTube channel connected through OAuth at most (RTMP destinations to YouTube are not counted). Not while live.

tools.name: stream_remove_output
tools.description: Unlinks a destination from the stream; one that is not linked is left as it is. Not while live; use stream_toggle_output.

tools.name: stream_toggle_output
tools.description: Enables or disables a linked destination without unlinking it. Disabling works while live and takes that destination off air; enabling does not work while live.

tools.name: stream_schedule
tools.description: Schedules the stream to start at a set time, optionally with an end and a repeat. Replaces any existing schedule.

tools.name: stream_cancel_schedule
tools.description: Removes the stream's schedule and repeat. A live session keeps running. The stream's streamDuration stays (stream_update streamDuration 0 removes it).

tools.name: stream_start
tools.description: Starts the stream now. It answers at once with state preparing; the stream goes preparing, activating, then active (on air) within about a minute: read it with stream_get, which also says why when it fails. Refused with STREAM_NOT_READY and the issues to fix when it is not ready, and while it is alr

tools.name: stream_stop
tools.description: Stops the stream: it goes off air on every destination and stops spending credits. Media, playlists and settings are kept. A schedule starts it again unless `cancelSchedule` is set. A scheduled stream that is not running yet is left as it is, unless `cancelSchedule` is set.

tools.name: stream_preflight_check
tools.description: Checks whether the stream can start, including whether the workspace has the credits for it, and returns the blocking issues with how to fix each. A few show only once an earlier one is fixed (sound is checked once there is video), so check again after fixing. It does not contact the destination: a

tools.name: destination_list
tools.description: Lists destinations (YouTube channels and custom RTMP endpoints) with their status. Stream keys are never returned.

tools.name: destination_connection_hints
tools.description: Returns how to connect a platform: its RTMP ingest URL, where the user finds the stream key, and platform limits. Use it before destination_create_rtmp; never guess an ingest URL.

tools.name: destination_create_rtmp
tools.description: Creates a destination from an RTMP URL and stream key (Twitch, Kick, Facebook, any RTMP server). A stream key backs one destination: the same key again is refused with the existing destination's id. The URL cannot be changed later (remove the destination and create it again); the key can, with desti

tools.name: destination_create_youtube_oauth
tools.description: Connects a YouTube channel through Google OAuth. Without `channelId` returns the consent URL for the user to open (valid for about 10 minutes), `channels` (authorized, with no destination yet: pass one's `channelId` to create it) and `connected` (channels that already are destinations); with `channe

tools.name: destination_update
tools.description: Renames a destination or replaces its RTMP stream key. A live stream uses the new key after a restart.

tools.name: destination_remove
tools.description: Removes a destination from the workspace; it no longer appears in destination_list, and every stream it was linked to loses that output (stream_get lists a stream's outputs). Refused while a live stream uses it. The channel or RTMP server itself is not touched.

tools.name: playlist_get
tools.description: Returns a playlist: its version, playing order (`mode`) and items (item id, media id, name, duration). Items come in their stored order: shuffle and custom play them in another order without reordering them here. Playlist ids come from stream_get.

tools.name: playlist_patch
tools.description: Adds, removes and reorders playlist items with a JSON Patch (RFC 6902) over the document playlist_get returns. All operations apply or none. Media must be ready (upload_get_import_job_state) and of the playlist's kind: video in a video playlist, audio in an audio one. `test` checks /version only, an

tools.name: playlist_copy
tools.description: Copies all items of one playlist into another, empty one of the same kind. The target also takes the source's sequential or shuffle setting; a custom order is never copied.

tools.name: playlist_set_playing_order
tools.description: Sets how a playlist plays: in order, shuffled, or by a custom order. See custom_order_* to create an arbitrary order defined by a script: it can pick the next item based on the time, the previously played item, and so on. For custom, `picks` are the first items it plays over the playlist as it is no

tools.name: custom_order_list
tools.description: Lists custom orders (playing-order rules written from a text description), or returns one with its rules when `id` is given.

tools.name: custom_order_create
tools.description: Creates a custom order from a description of how the playlist should play, e.g. "start with the intro, never two songs in a row". Apply it with playlist_set_playing_order.

tools.name: custom_order_refine
tools.description: Changes a custom order with an instruction in words. Playlists using it pick up the change.

tools.name: upload_list
tools.description: Lists uploaded media (video, audio, images) with size, duration (milliseconds) and whether it is ready to play.

tools.name: upload_get_upload_url
tools.description: Creates a media record and returns the URL(s) to PUT the file to; the URLs stop working after 11 hours. After the PUT (after the last part, for multipart) call upload_get_import_job_state until it reports ready: that also assembles a multipart upload. For a file that is already online, use upload_im

tools.name: upload_import_from_url
tools.description: Imports media from a URL: a video page (YouTube, Vimeo, Twitch, …) or a direct file link. Runs in the background; follow it with upload_get_import_job_state.

tools.name: upload_get_import_job_state
tools.description: Returns whether media is ready to play, for an import and for a direct upload alike: progress and error, then its duration (milliseconds) and resolution (null when not measured). `ready` is true only once the file has been analysed; call again while it is false and `error` is null. status `failed` w

tools.name: upload_remove
tools.description: Deletes media: video, audio or an image. Refused with IN_USE, naming what uses it when known, while a playlist uses it; an image also while it is a stream's YouTube thumbnail or while the workspace has scenes. Media already removed answers removed:true again.

tools.name: account_get
tools.description: Returns the account, its workspace and its money. `billing.balance` is US dollars and `creditsLeft` the same amount in credits (1,000,000 credits = $1); `goodStanding` false means streams cannot start until credits are added. `spend` is the burn rate now and `running` each stream that is on air now,

tools.name: scene_get
tools.description: Reads a live scene by path. Start with `*`: it returns the resource types (frame, source, component, element, …) and their definitions, which describe everything else. Reads the draft unless `state` or `revision` is given.

tools.name: scene_set
tools.description: Creates or changes one resource in the scene draft. `replace` writes the whole resource (read its type with scene_get first for the shape); `merge` changes only the fields given and keeps the rest. Send one of them. Where a scene_get answer says `value` or `edits`, that is `replace` and `merge` here

tools.name: scene_remove
tools.description: Removes a resource from the scene draft. Refused when something else uses it.

tools.name: scene_list_revisions
tools.description: Lists the scene's published revisions, newest first.

tools.name: scene_publish
tools.description: Publishes the scene draft; streams playing the scene show it at once. Refused with SCENE_INVALID and the problems to fix.

tools.name: scene_rollback_to_revision
tools.description: Publishes an earlier revision again as a new revision; streams playing the scene show it at once. The draft is not changed: it still holds the latest edits.

tools.name: scene_get_live_state
tools.description: Reads what the scene has on air: each stream the scene is set on, with online (whether that stream is on air now) and, while it is, the frame on air, the frame cued next, the controls' values, each source's status and what its playlists play. Empty when no stream has the scene.

tools.name: scene_control_live
tools.description: Acts on the scene on air, as its operator would; viewers see it at once. goFrame takes a frame to air, next cues one, setControl sets a control, setData replaces a table's rows, skip moves a playlist source to its next item. Changes what is on air, never the draft. The answer is the state after the

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: stream_start, stream_preflight_check, destination_create_youtube_oauth, upload_get_upload_url · Private data: stream_preflight_check, playlist_patch, upload_get_upload_url, upload_import_from_url, upload_get_import_job_state · Public sink: stream_update_youtube_broadcast_settings, upload_list, upload_get_upload_url, upload_import_from_url, upload_get_import_job_state, upload_remove, scene_set, scene_publish · Destructive: stream_remove, stream_remove_output, destination_create_rtmp, destination_remove, upload_get_import_job_state, upload_remove, scene_remove.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: stream_start, stream_preflight_check, destination_create_youtube_oauth, upload_get_upload_url · Private data: stream_preflight_check, playlist_patch, upload_get_upload_url, upload_import_from_url, upload_get_import_job_state · Public sink: stream_update_youtube_broadcast_settings, upload_list, upload_get_upload_url, upload_import_from_url, upload_get_import_job_state, upload_remove, scene_set, scene_publish · Destructive: stream_remove, stream_remove_output, destination_create_rtmp, destination_remove, upload_get_import_job_state, upload_remove, scene_remove

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "scene_get" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Read the scene's draft (or a published version, with version): a resource (with its revision and children, the sub-paths to read next), a type such as element/Text or source/data (its props), a mask ending in /* (a list), or "" (the types). as: "image" on a frame or layer → a picture of it. Several " → after: "Reads a live scene by path. Start with `*`: it returns the resource types (frame, source, component, element, …) and their definitions, which describe everything else. Reads the draft unless `state` or `revision` is given."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

evidence.snippet: before: "Delete whole resources (frames, layers, sources, components). All or nothing: anything in use by something not removed in the same call is refused, with what uses it. (In a scene's draft; scene: its id.) Removing a resource needs its revision in `revisions` (path → the revision you read; "*": whatev" → after: "Removes a resource from the scene draft. Refused when something else uses it."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

evidence.snippet: before: "Create, replace or change one resource; get <type> shows what each takes, with an example. value is the whole resource, as get answers it: a frame { code: "<JSX>" } or, as JSON, { name, root }; a component { description, props, tsx }; a source or table its fields. edits change part of it: [{ old, ne" → after: "Creates or changes one resource in the scene draft. `replace` writes the whole resource (read its type with scene_get first for the shape); `merge` changes only the fields given and keeps the rest. Send one of them. Where a scene_get answer says `value` or `edits`, that is `replace` and `merge` here"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
